photos.question: A client receives IV vancomycin every 12 hours. When should the nurse draw the trough level?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #301!

🧪 Peak or trough? Timing the vancomycin lab matters!

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Within 30 minutes before the next dose

🧠 Rationale: The trough is the lowest drug level in the blood.

It is drawn just before the next dose, usually within 30 minutes.

Drawing it at the wrong time gives a false result and a wrong dose change.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Vancomycin

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Glycopeptide antibiotic (used for MRSA and C. diff)

⚠️ Adverse Effects:

🔹 Kidney injury (nephrotoxicity)

🔹 Hearing loss or ringing in the ears

🔹 Flushing and rash if infused too fast

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Infuse slowly, over at least 60 minutes

✅ Monitor creatinine and urine output

✅ Time trough draws right before the dose

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Trough = Toward the next dose. Lowest level, last minute!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Where should the nurse place the stethoscope to best hear the mitral valve?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #302!

❤️ Can you find the mitral valve on the chest?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac assessment question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — 5th intercostal space, left midclavicular line

🧠 Rationale: The mitral valve is best heard at the apex of the heart.

This is the 5th intercostal space at the left midclavicular line.

It is also where the apical pulse is counted.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Heart Sound Landmarks

🩺 Valve Areas:

🔹 Aortic: 2nd ICS, right sternal border

🔹 Pulmonic: 2nd ICS, left sternal border

🔹 Tricuspid: 4th ICS, left lower sternal border

🔹 Mitral: 5th ICS, left midclavicular line

🔊 Heart Sounds:

🔹 S1 (lub) is loudest at the apex

🔹 S2 (dub) is loudest at the base

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Count the apical pulse for a full minute

✅ Listen with the diaphragm, then the bell

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

All People Enjoy Time Magazine: Aortic, Pulmonic, Erb's point, Tricuspid, Mitral!

photos.question: Which assessment finding best shows that a client needs airway suctioning?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #303!

🫁 When does your client actually need suctioning?

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Coarse crackles over the large airways

🧠 Rationale: Coarse crackles (rhonchi) mean secretions are in the large airways.

Suction is done based on assessment, not on a set schedule.

The other findings are normal and do not need suctioning.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Airway Suctioning

⚠️ Signs a Client Needs Suctioning:

🔹 Coarse crackles or gurgling

🔹 Visible secretions

🔹 Falling SpO2

🔹 Restlessness or increased work of breathing

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Preoxygenate before suctioning

✅ Suction no longer than 10 to 15 seconds

✅ Apply suction only while pulling out

✅ Reassess breath sounds after

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Hear the gurgle, clear the gurgle!

photos.question: Which lab results should the nurse expect in a client with primary hyperparathyroidism?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #304!

🦴 Calcium and phosphorus: which way do they go?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — High calcium, low phosphorus

🧠 Rationale: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) pulls calcium out of the bones.

PTH also makes the kidneys get rid of phosphorus.

Calcium and phosphorus move in opposite directions.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Hyperparathyroidism

⚠️ Signs and Symptoms:

🔹 Kidney stones

🔹 Bone pain and fractures

🔹 Muscle weakness and fatigue

🔹 Constipation and confusion

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Encourage fluids to prevent stones

✅ Strain urine if stones suspected

✅ Fall and fracture precautions

✅ Monitor calcium levels

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Stones, bones, groans and moans: high calcium!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Endocrine #Parathyroid #Calcium #Electrolytes #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: Parents ask how long their toddler should ride in a rear-facing car seat. Which response is best?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #305!

🚗 Rear-facing car seats: when is it safe to turn around?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric safety question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — As long as possible, until the seat's limits

🧠 Rationale: Rear-facing seats protect the head, neck and spine in a crash.

Children should stay rear-facing until they reach the seat's height or weight limit.

Most children can stay rear-facing well past age 2.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Car Seat Safety

🚸 Key Points:

🔹 Rear-facing as long as the seat allows

🔹 Then forward-facing with a harness

🔹 Then a booster seat until the seat belt fits

🔹 Back seat until at least age 13

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Harness snug at the collarbone

✅ Chest clip at armpit level

✅ No bulky coats under the harness

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Rear-facing is the safest-facing!

photos.question: A client at 30 weeks of pregnancy is in preterm labor. Which medication helps the baby's lungs mature?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #306!

🤰 Preterm labor at 30 weeks: which drug protects the baby's lungs?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Betamethasone

🧠 Rationale: Betamethasone is a corticosteroid given to the mother.

It speeds up fetal lung maturity and surfactant production.

It lowers the risk of newborn respiratory distress syndrome.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Betamethasone in Preterm Labor

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Corticosteroid

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Fetal lung maturity, usually 24 to 34 weeks

🔹 Given IM, 2 doses 24 hours apart

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Raised blood glucose in the mother

🧠 Do Not Confuse:

🔹 Magnesium sulfate protects the fetal brain

🔹 Oxytocin and methylergonovine are for contractions and bleeding

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Beta for Breathing: betamethasone builds baby's lungs!

photos.question: An older adult is newly confused. Which finding suggests delirium rather than dementia?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #307!

🧠 Delirium or dementia? This one shows up on the NCLEX a lot!

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Sudden onset over hours to days

🧠 Rationale: Delirium comes on suddenly, over hours to days.

It is often caused by infection, drugs, dehydration or low oxygen.

It is usually reversible once the cause is treated.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Delirium vs Dementia

⚡ Delirium:

🔹 Sudden onset

🔹 Attention changes and fluctuates

🔹 Often reversible

🐢 Dementia:

🔹 Slow, gradual decline

🔹 Attention intact early

🔹 Progressive, not reversible

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Report new confusion right away

✅ Look for the cause: UTI, meds, hypoxia

✅ Reorient, keep a calm, safe room

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Delirium is Dramatic and Sudden. Dementia is Drawn out!
